proposals: MoSPI should publish the GDP deflator itself as a series in its API, annual and quarterly, alongside the nominal and real GDP data, so analysts measuring the rupee's real value do not have to back out India's inflation from growth rates, as this piece had to.

The RBI should publish a bilateral real rupee–dollar exchange rate alongside its trade-weighted REER, with the deflators and base period stated, so the split between inflation-offsetting depreciation and the roughly 27% real loss in buying power is an official figure rather than a reader's calculation.

The RBI should publish, next to its weekly reserves data, a ready-computed trailing 12-month net foreign-currency purchase or sale figure as a share of GDP, so anyone can check directly whether intervention runs in the direction the US Treasury's third test is designed to catch.

The Finance Ministry's Economic Survey should include each year a decomposition of the rupee's move against the dollar into the inflation differential and the real change, so public debate does not treat a nominal fall, such as the 11.9% over the last twelve months, as wholly real or wholly inflationary.
